why: The bright gold porthole ring with the lantern-lit stern inside, and the dark sea just starting to bleed in behind it, reads as an iris about to open onto the whole scene. The big empty left half still feels underused.

The storm wave turning into a glowing equity-curve line that peels back to reveal a classroom bench is the cleverest image in the set: markets as weather. The heading '3 IDIOTS / The Workshop' and the caption 'THE KRAKEN'S STORM · PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN' contradict each other mid-transition.
A burn hole eating through the RDR camp plate is a dramatic 'something is coming through' moment. The 'HARRY POTTER' heading over an RDR plate and an RDR caption is confusing for a beat.
Big western wood-type title over a sepia tintype in a cream mount, like a period photograph; calm and confident, and it makes me want to see what the 'act' holds.
A white lightning-edged tear splitting a misty classroom from a teal storm sea is dramatic and clearly in motion. Same heading/caption mismatch (3 Idiots heading, Pirates caption).
Same tintype as H004. Still handsome, though it is a static frame and relies on the type to pull me on.
Pure black page with a title top-left and a small ship porthole bottom-right; nothing behind the porthole yet. It reads as a page that hasn't finished loading rather than an opening shot.
The burn hole now shows a single candle flame inside: a sharp tease of the next world (Hogwarts candles) through the last one (the camp). Heading/caption mismatch remains.
